results.content: The University of Michigan's preliminary consumer sentiment index fell to 51.0 in August from 55.2 in July, the first decline in three months and well below the 54.5 consensus forecast. The drop was broad-based, with Republicans showing the steepest decline — sentiment in that group is now 19% below pre-Iran conflict levels and at its lowest since the 2024 election. Year-ahead inflation expectations rose to 4.3% from 4.2%, while long-term expectations held at 3.3%. results.title: US Consumer Sentiment Slumps to 51 in August as Inflation Fears Resurface

results.content:
The University of Michigan's Surveys of ​Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped ​to 51.0 this month from 55.2 in ⁠July, ending two straight months of improvement. ​Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the index ​would be at 54.5.

The decline in sentiment occurred across the political spectrum, with an especially big ​month-to-month drop among Republicans.
results.title: US consumer sentiment deteriorates in August

results.content: In a separate report, the University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped to 51.0 this month from 55.2 in July, ending two straight months of improvement. Sentiment deteriorated across the political spectrum, with an especially big month-to-month drop ​among Republicans, a potential sign of trouble for President Donald Trump's party as it seeks to retain control of the U.S. Congress in the November midterm elections.
